title: Travel Protection Plans: Valuation Standard for an Open Travel Credit
content:
A future travel credit standing open against the linked vacation package, one of the Vacation Package Products, is valued at a share when a cancellation claim is rated on a Travel Protection Plans certificate. Two things decide that share: whether the credit may be transferred to another traveller, and whether it may be redeemed after the last day of the journey insured.

Where the credit standing open against the package may be transferred to another traveller and it may be redeemed after the last day of the journey insured, a credit is valued at the whole of it, 100 per cent.

Where the credit standing open against the package may not be transferred and it may be redeemed after the last day of the journey insured, a credit is valued at 80 per cent.

Where neither holds, a credit is valued at nothing, 0 per cent.

## The graded valuation

| Transferable to another traveller | Redeemable after the last day of the journey insured | A credit is valued at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yes | Yes | 100 per cent |
| No | Yes | 80 per cent |
| Either way | No | 0 per cent |

## Cases

A case at full value: the package's credit may be passed to another traveller and its expiry falls after the last day of the journey insured. It is worth its face amount to the traveller and is valued at 100 per cent.

A case at four fifths: the credit is tied to this traveller and cannot be passed on, but it still expires after the last day of the journey insured. It is valued at 80 per cent.

A case at nothing: the credit expires on or before the last day of the journey insured. Neither of the first two cases is reached, whether the credit may be transferred or not, and it is valued at 0 per cent.

Hypothetically, a credit of 900.00 USD standing open is worth 900.00 USD at the full share, 720.00 USD at four fifths, and 0.00 USD where it cannot be redeemed after the last day of the journey insured.
